brief.situation: You are the security architect on call for Pemberly Foods, a fictional bakery manufacturer. At 02:00 EDR raises ransomware staging on the IT file servers, launched by the packaging-line vendor's remote-support account, which signed in through the VPN at 01:20. Three lines are running the night shift. Protect the plant, contain, keep evidence and report.
handover: Operators have rehearsed running the lines in manual. A zero-trust access broker is deployed for staff applications but vendors still use the VPN.
A microsegmentation policy for the IT server VLAN is written and tested but not enforced.
howItWorks: Each task takes analyst time: choose it, then let the work finish, which moves the clock by the minutes that task takes. The attacker keeps working on the same clock.
New alerts and log lines appear in the console as they happen.
When you declare the incident contained, you notify, write the record and explain your reasoning.

reviewEntry.label: Review the VPN appliance and EDR for how they got in

effects.finding: vendor-acme signed in at 01:20 from 198.51.100.120, outside the vendor's window, with a password unchanged since 2023 and no MFA; the appliance firmware is behind. From FILE02 the account is enumerating the domain.

mapPaths.label: Map every path from IT into the plant (firewall rules, dual-homed hosts)

effects.finding: HIST01, the historian, has one network leg in the IT server VLAN and one in the plant control network, reachable on RDP and SMB from IT. There is no DMZ: that host is the bridge.

cutVpn.label: Take the VPN appliance offline and move vendors to the zero-trust access broker

effects.log: The appliance is off the internet. Staff use the access broker with MFA per application; vendor-acme has no broker access.

cutConduit.label: Close the IT-to-OT conduit: historian data out through the DMZ only, nothing in

effects.log: At the plant firewall, nothing from IT reaches the control network; historian data goes out one way to a DMZ replica.
HIST01 is isolated; the plant keeps running, trending is unavailable until a clean historian is up.

islandOt.label: Island the plant control network and run the lines in manual

effects.log: The control network is physically islanded and operators run the lines in manual, as rehearsed.
Every line is stopped to a safe state; product in progress is scrapped.

isolateBackups.label: Cut the backup server's admin plane off the domain

effects.log: The backup server answers only its own local administrators from the backup VLAN; domain accounts cannot manage it.

microsegment.label: Apply the prepared microsegmentation policy to the IT server VLAN

effects.log: East-west SMB, RDP and remote service traffic between IT servers is now denied except where a rule names it.

effects.log: vendor-acme is disabled, every Domain Admin password is reset and the ticket-granting key is reset twice.

writeup.question: For the incident record: what you protected first and why, how you separated the plant without stopping it, and what the architecture must change.

parts.label: Priorities
parts.criteria: Protects safety and the plant first (the IT-to-OT path), then the backups (recovery), then closes the entry and the stolen admin rights; mentions why a full shutdown is not the default when manual operation is rehearsed.
parts.modelAnswer: The plant and its people come first, so I closed the only path into the control network, then cut the backups off the domain so we could recover, then shut the VPN and reset the stolen admin rights. Islanding and manual running were rehearsed, so a full shutdown was not needed.

parts.label: Segmentation
parts.criteria: Identifies the dual-homed historian as the flat path; closes it with a DMZ one-way flow or isolation; uses microsegmentation to stop east-west spread on IT.
parts.modelAnswer: HIST01 had a leg on both networks with RDP and SMB open from IT. Closing the conduit and sending historian data one way through the DMZ removed that bridge; the microsegmentation policy stopped server-to-server spread on IT.

parts.label: Architecture change
parts.criteria: Proposes a DMZ between IT and OT with no dual-homed hosts, vendor access through a zero-trust broker with MFA per application, and an offline or isolated backup admin plane; keeps evidence of the entry point before resetting it.
parts.modelAnswer: No host should sit on both networks: data crosses through a DMZ. Vendors come in through the broker with MFA to named applications only, and the backup admin plane stays off the domain. I imaged the appliance before resetting it.

expertPath.text: Call the incident commander and the plant manager; map the IT-to-OT paths: the dual-homed historian is the bridge.
Close the conduit (historian data out through the DMZ only); cut the backup server's admin plane off the domain.
Take the VPN offline and reset vendor-acme and every Domain Admin credential; enforce the microsegmentation policy.
Image the appliance and collect FILE02 before any reset or rebuild.
Notify executives, the plant manager, legal, the insurer and CISA; record the vendor VPN account and the DMZ change.

contained.headline: Good: the bridge first
contained.body: At a plant, the first question is what can reach the control network. You found the dual-homed historian, closed it, saved the backups and kept the lines running.

containedCostly.headline: Contained, at a cost
containedCostly.body: The plant is safe. The criteria show what cost you: a full shutdown that manual running would have avoided, IT encryption, or time.

otHit.headline: The plant was reached
otHit.body: Work on IT alone left the historian bridging into the control network. Close the IT-to-OT path first (CISA: segment IT and OT, use a DMZ).

backupsLost.headline: Backups deleted
backupsLost.body: A domain-joined backup server is managed by whoever holds Domain Admin. Cut its admin plane off before the attacker reaches it.

evidenceLost.headline: Entry point wiped
evidenceLost.body: Image the appliance before resetting it; it holds how the account was used and whether the appliance itself is implanted.

stillIn.headline: Closed too soon
stillIn.body: Shutting the VPN does not undo Domain Admin rights already taken, and a foothold on the historian survives losing the VPN.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: With an intruder in IT, the architecture question is what bridges into the plant: here, a historian with a leg on both networks. Close that path first (one-way through the DMZ, isolate the historian, or island the plant and run in manual, as rehearsed) rather than shutting the plant down, cut the backups' admin plane off the domain, take the VPN offline and reset the vendor and Domain Admin credentials, enforce microsegmentation on IT, and image the appliance before resetting it. Afterwards: a DMZ with no dual-homed hosts and vendor access through a zero-trust broker with MFA.
